senses.definition: departing from what is normal or expected
senses.example: The researchers threw out one aberrant reading caused by a faulty sensor.

senses.definition: to choose not to do or have something, especially something enjoyable
senses.example: She abstained from sweets for the whole month of training.

senses.definition: to formally decline to vote
senses.example: Three members abstained, so the motion passed by a single vote.

senses.definition: enthusiastic public praise
senses.example: Her first novel won wide acclaim from critics and readers alike.

senses.definition: to praise publicly and enthusiastically
senses.example: The bridge was acclaimed as a triumph of engineering.

senses.definition: open to more than one interpretation; not clear
senses.example: The contract's ambiguous wording led to a long dispute.

senses.definition: having mixed or contradictory feelings about something
senses.example: He felt ambivalent about the move: excited by the job, sad to leave his friends.

senses.definition: lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern
senses.example: Low turnout was blamed on voter apathy.

senses.definition: understood by few; mysterious or secret
senses.example: The tax code is full of arcane rules that only specialists follow.

senses.definition: showing an insensitive and cruel disregard for others
senses.example: The callous remark about the victims caused an outcry.

senses.definition: a person or thing that precipitates an event or change
senses.example: The letter was the catalyst for a wave of protests.

senses.definition: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without itself changing
senses.example: Platinum acts as a catalyst in the car's exhaust system.

senses.definition: to come together to form one mass or whole
senses.example: The scattered protest groups coalesced into a single movement.

senses.definition: corresponding in size or degree; in proportion
senses.example: The salary will be commensurate with experience.

senses.definition: showing smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements
senses.example: After three easy wins, the team grew complacent and lost the final.

senses.definition: intended to placate or pacify
senses.example: After the argument he sent a conciliatory note and a bunch of flowers.

senses.definition: giving a lot of information clearly and in few words
senses.example: Write a concise summary of no more than a page.

senses.definition: a confusing and difficult problem or question
senses.example: How to fund the new library without raising taxes was a real conundrum.

senses.definition: deserving blame
senses.example: The inquiry found the builder culpable for the collapse.

senses.definition: hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed
senses.example: A cursory glance at the report missed the main error.

senses.definition: to describe or portray something precisely
senses.example: The plan clearly delineates who is responsible for each task.

senses.definition: to indicate the exact position of a border or boundary
senses.example: Stones delineate the edge of the old churchyard.

senses.definition: to criticize unfairly; to disparage
senses.example: He denigrated his rival's work to make his own look better.

senses.definition: to express contempt for; to ridicule
senses.example: Critics derided the film as a waste of a fine cast.

senses.definition: to regard or represent as being of little worth
senses.example: It is easy to disparage an idea you haven't tried.

senses.definition: essentially different in kind; not able to be compared
senses.example: The anthology brings together disparate voices from across the century.

senses.definition: temporarily inactive or asleep
senses.example: The volcano has been dormant for two hundred years.

senses.definition: regularly found among particular people or in a certain area
senses.example: Malaria is endemic in parts of the region.

senses.definition: (of a plant or animal) native and restricted to a certain place
senses.example: The lemur is endemic to Madagascar.

senses.definition: intended for or understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge
senses.example: The novel is full of esoteric references to medieval theology.

senses.definition: a mild or indirect word or expression used in place of one thought too harsh or blunt
senses.example: "Passed away" is a common euphemism for "died."

senses.definition: (of a price or amount) unreasonably high
senses.example: The hotel charged an exorbitant fee for a bottle of water.

senses.definition: to make an action or process easier
senses.example: The new software facilitates communication between departments.

senses.definition: having or displaying a passionate intensity
senses.example: She was a fervent supporter of the local theater.

senses.definition: diverse in character or content
senses.example: The class was a heterogeneous mix of ages and backgrounds.

senses.definition: deliberate exaggeration not meant to be taken literally
senses.example: Saying the line was a mile long was hyperbole, but it was long.

senses.definition: not showing due respect for another person; impertinent
senses.example: The impudent boy stuck out his tongue at the teacher.

senses.definition: lacking flavor
senses.example: The soup was insipid and needed salt.

senses.definition: lacking vigor or interest
senses.example: The movie's insipid dialogue bored even the actors.

senses.definition: ignorant of or uninterested in cultures, ideas or peoples outside one's own experience
senses.example: The village was insular and suspicious of newcomers.

senses.definition: feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph
senses.example: Jubilant fans poured onto the field after the final whistle.

senses.definition: a person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society
senses.example: The misanthrope in the story lives alone on a remote island.

senses.definition: showing a lack of experience, wisdom or judgment
senses.example: It was naive to think the problem would solve itself.

senses.definition: famous or well known, typically for some bad quality or deed
senses.example: The road is notorious for accidents.

senses.definition: new or unusual in an interesting way
senses.example: The team took a novel approach to the problem.

senses.definition: not discovered or known about; uncertain
senses.example: The origins of the custom are obscure.

senses.definition: not important or well known
senses.example: The prize went to an obscure poet from a small town.

senses.definition: to keep from being seen; to conceal
senses.example: Clouds obscured the summit.

senses.definition: no longer produced or used; out of date
senses.example: Typewriters became obsolete when personal computers arrived.

senses.definition: spending money or resources freely and recklessly
senses.example: The prodigal heir spent his fortune in two years.

senses.definition: having or giving something on a lavish scale
senses.example: The garden was prodigal with roses every June.

senses.definition: in a state or period of inactivity or dormancy
senses.example: The disease can remain quiescent for years.

senses.definition: to consign or dismiss to an inferior rank or position
senses.example: The old furniture was relegated to the basement.

senses.definition: the art of effective or persuasive speaking or writing
senses.example: She studied rhetoric to improve her debating.

senses.definition: language designed to persuade or impress, often regarded as lacking sincerity or meaningful content
senses.example: Voters were tired of empty campaign rhetoric.

senses.definition: not being what it purports to be; false or fake
senses.example: The study was based on spurious data.

senses.definition: (of reasoning) apparently but not actually valid
senses.example: He made a spurious connection between the two events.

senses.definition: unnecessary, especially through being more than enough
senses.example: The design avoids superfluous decoration.

senses.definition: (of a remark or idea) overused and consequently of little import
senses.example: The card had a trite message about following your dreams.

senses.definition: never done or known before
senses.example: The drought caused unprecedented damage to the crops.

senses.definition: to regard with great respect; to revere
senses.example: The village venerates the old monk as a saint.
